typology.definition: A state's capacity to develop, run and govern AI on infrastructure, data and models it controls, rather than renting them from foreign providers. Definitions are contested: 'hard' sovereignty means self-sufficiency across the stack; 'soft' sovereignty means control over the layers that matter for a given use case.

sources.value: McKinsey: four components - territorial, operational, technological, legal
CSET: five-layer stack - energy, chips, infrastructure, models, applications - plus talent, capital, research, governance, security

typology.definition: Domestic data centres and GPU clusters under national legal control, funded by budgets, state banks or sovereign-wealth vehicles.
typology.caveat: Hosting is not ownership: Malaysia hosts ~9% of Epoch-tracked frontier compute, largely for foreign tenants; France's 'sovereign' Campus AI is 70% owned by Abu Dhabi's MGX.

typology.definition: Foundation models pre-trained from random initialisation by a national lab or champion.

typology.term: Sovereign models - adapted (continued pre-training / fine-tune of foreign open weights)
typology.definition: A national model built on a foreign open-weight base (Llama, Gemma, Qwen, Mistral, Nemotron) with local data.

share.value: 56% of sovereign LLMs; Llama 38%, Qwen 20%, Mistral 19% of adapted

typology.caveat: Inherits the base model's licence, training-data and alignment choices; an AIES paper calls fine-tune-only sovereignty 'sovereignty theater'. Korea disqualified Naver for unmodified Qwen encoder weights (Jan 2026). Supply risk: CNAS (26 Oct 2026) warns top open-weight releases may dry up as Beijing drafts export controls covering model weights (MOFCOM/MOST draft 16 Oct 2026, comments to 15 Nov 2026).

typology.definition: Foreign proprietary or open models run in-country under local data residency, often via 'sovereign cloud' offers.
examples: Japan's 'Gennai' government AI (OpenAI-powered, now A/B-testing domestic LLMs)
SoftBank Cloud PF Type A on Oracle Alloy
typology.caveat: Stanford HAI (Jul 2026 brief): big-tech sovereignty offerings may reconfigure rather than remove dependency.

typology.definition: Legal and practical control over national training corpora and the data pipeline (licensed national-library, news and administrative text).
examples: GPT-NL licensed news + KB national library

typology.definition: Public money behind the stack: budgets/appropriations, equity funds, sovereign-wealth vehicles, and mobilisation headlines - four categories that must never be summed.
Markets where foreign assistants are blocked or restricted, so domestic models dominate regardless of policy intent.
examples: Russia (sanctions): domestic share depends on measurement method

typology.term: Popularity metrics (and why they cannot be compared)
typology.definition: Hugging Face downloads (developer pulls, inflated by CI/mirrors), derivatives (fine-tunes on a base), app MAU/WAU (consumer reach; panels disagree), web-traffic share, Statcounter referral share (clicks from chatbots to websites), OpenRouter token share (one developer aggregator), leaderboard rank (capability, not use).
typology.caveat: Report each metric with its scope; never mix WAU with MAU or HF-only with all-channel downloads.
